_provenance.what: What the uploaded Santhanam edition attests: which chapters exist, the highest verse legibly read in each, and which verse markers were read at all.
_provenance.why: Citations in this project are keyed to Santhanam's English chapter-and-verse numbering, so this is the witness they actually point at. citation-verify.mjs resolves every citation against it instead of trusting the string.
_provenance.source: BPHS-Santhanam-Vol-1.pdf and BPHS-Santhanam-Vol-2.pdf, the project's own uploads, read out as text.
_provenance.notTheMula: The Sanskrit mula was the intended witness and is NOT used: sa.wikisource.org is not on this environment's fetch allowlist and sanskritdocuments.org disallows robots. No workaround was attempted. It would also have needed a reconciliation pass between the mula's verse numbering and Santhanam's, and that pass would itself have been the unverified step.
_provenance.strength: THREE THINGS OF DECREASING STRENGTH. 'chapters' and the volume split are stated in both prefaces and are strong. 'verseMax' is a BOUND from the highest marker legibly read, not a verse count: the real chapter is at least that long. 'attested' is INCOMPLETE BY CONSTRUCTION, because this is OCR of a scanned printing in which verse 1 of chapter 46 reads 't.', 6-11 reads '6-ll.' and 44-49 reads '4449.'. A citation missing from 'attested' has not been shown wrong and has not been shown right; it belongs in a pending list saying so.
_provenance.noTextStored: Verse TEXT is not stored, only structure and hashes. The check this witness has to support is resolution — does the cited chapter and verse exist — and that needs structure, not text. It also keeps a scanned edition out of a public repository.
_provenance.volumeSplitSource: BPHS-Santhanam Vol. 1, preface: "The present volume—first volume—contains 45 chapters while the remaining 52 chapters have been put in the second volume." Vol. 2 opens at Chapter 46, "Dasas (Periods) of planets".
_provenance.resolutionNotes: A citation whose verse MARKER the scan lost but whose CONTENT is found in the chapter anyway. Each names a phrase that must appear there; the builder checks it, so the exception is verified and not merely asserted.

resolutions.why: the verse marker is lost in a run of unrecoverable Devanagari, so the chapter's legible bound stops at 10
resolutions.reasoning: the Kemadruma passage the citation is used for appears in chapter 37 directly after verse 10, which is where vv. 11-13 fall; the content is attested where the number is not
